provider: Florida Department of Education, Office of Student Financial Assistance
name: Florida Bright Futures: Florida Academic Scholars (FAS)
value: Published 2026-27 funding covers 100% of tuition and specified mandatory fees at Florida public institutions, with comparable private-institution funding. A top FAS student in each district receives an additional per-credit award. Normally up to five years from graduation and 120 semester hours, with approved extended-hour/deferment exceptions. Institutional disbursement after drop/add; renewal requires 3.0 unrounded/unweighted cumulative college GPA and earned hours appropriate to funded load. 2027-28 funding amounts are not yet published.
deadline: For 2027 graduates, submit FFAA October 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027. Qualifying tests must be taken by August 31, 2027; other requirements by graduation. Mid-year graduates seeking immediate spring funding must apply by December 31 of their senior year and test by January 31. Time zone/time not stated.
apply: Submit Florida Financial Aid Application, then track OSFA award status and keep institution information current. School supplies official transcript; arrange official ACT/CLT/SAT reporting and signed service/work documentation. Nontraditional applicants must arrange official transcripts and any required home-school/GED/out-of-state documentation. No annual FFAA for continued renewal.
eligibility: Florida resident and U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen; standard Florida diploma/equivalent or eligible nontraditional route. Standard FAS path requires 16 specified college-preparatory credits, 3.50 weighted Bright Futures GPA, and ACT 29, CLT 95 or SAT 1330 for 2026-27 graduates seeking fall 2027 funding. Complete 100 volunteer hours, 100 paid-work hours, or 100 combined hours. National Merit, AICE and IB recognition have alternative routes; AP Capstone Diploma can qualify for FAS. Enrol in an eligible Florida degree/certificate programme, normally at least six non-remedial credits per term. Felony restriction with clemency exception applies.
notes: Standard GPA and test thresholds have merit-recognition exceptions, so no universal GPA filter is applied. Non-Florida high-school route requires Florida-resident parent/guardian military or public-service assignment away from Florida, including specified recent retirees. Dropped/withdrawn courses after drop/add normally require repayment before renewal; documented emergency appeals and limited restoration are available. Requirements/funding may change with legislation.

Enrol in an eligible Florida degree/certificate programme, normally at least six non-remedial credits per term. Felony restriction with clemency exception applies.
notes: Standard GPA and test thresholds have merit-recognition exceptions, so no universal GPA filter is applied. name: HOPE Scholarship
value: Institution-specific undergraduate tuition award for up to 15 credit hours per term at eligible Georgia public institutions; private-institution amounts based on half/full-time attendance, up to 12 hours. Normally ends at a bachelor degree, 127 attempted/combined-paid semester hours (190 quarter), or ten years after high-school completion for new recipients. Renewal requires 3.0 calculated college HOPE GPA at specified checkpoints and satisfactory academic progress. Current linked amount table covers 2026-27; fall 2027 rates require confirmation.
deadline: Apply by the last day of the school term or withdrawal date, whichever occurs first. College-specific additional application/deadline requirements may apply. Apply early; there is no single statewide calendar date.
apply: Complete FAFSA annually or online Georgia Student Finance Application (GSFAPP), plus any college-specific steps. Georgia accredited schools electronically report transcripts/rigor data; out-of-state or nonaccredited/home-study routes need official manual-evaluation documents and qualifying test reporting where applicable. Monitor GAfutures eligibility and college financial-aid office.
eligibility: Georgia resident under institution rules (normally 12 months if resident at high-school completion, otherwise a 24-month route; dependent/private-school rules differ), U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen, undergraduate degree student at eligible Georgia institution. Meet applicable Selective Service, loan/refund good-standing, drug-free and satisfactory-progress rules. Standard accredited high-school/home-study route: minimum 3.0 calculated HOPE GPA and four academic-rigor credits. Ineligible-school/unaccredited-home-study or TCSG HSE route may qualify by ACT 24 or SAT 1160 before completion without that high-school GPA route. College students may gain eligibility at 30/60/90 semester-hour checkpoints with 3.0 calculated college HOPE GPA.
notes: Calculated HOPE GPA differs from school GPA: school weighting removed, limited 0.5 AP/IB/degree-level dual-enrolment weighting restored below A; honors not weighted, no rounding, with approved advanced fine arts counted starting class of 2027. Alternate routes prevent a universal high-school GPA filter. One regain opportunity at an attempted-hours checkpoint; military/disability time-limit extensions may apply. Private colleges require at least six credits; public institutions have no minimum credit load.

name: Zell Miller Scholarship
value: Institution-specific undergraduate tuition award for up to 15 credit hours per term at eligible Georgia public institutions; private-institution amounts based on half/full-time attendance, up to 12 hours. Normally ends at a bachelor degree, 127 attempted/combined-paid semester hours (190 quarter), or ten years after high-school completion for new recipients. Renewal requires 3.3 calculated college HOPE GPA at specified checkpoints and satisfactory academic progress. Current linked amount table covers 2026-27; fall 2027 rates require confirmation.
deadline: Apply by the last day of the school term or withdrawal date, whichever occurs first. College-specific additional application/deadline requirements may apply. Apply early; there is no single statewide calendar date.
apply: Complete FAFSA annually or online Georgia Student Finance Application (GSFAPP), plus any college-specific steps. Monitor GAfutures eligibility and college financial-aid office.
eligibility: Georgia resident under institution rules (normally 12 months if resident at high-school completion, otherwise a 24-month route; dependent/private-school rules differ), U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen, undergraduate degree student at eligible Georgia institution. Standard accredited high-school/home-study route: 3.7 calculated HOPE GPA, four rigor credits and single-administration SAT 1200 or current ACT equivalent 25 before graduation. Named valedictorian/salutatorian route uses 3.0 HOPE GPA and four rigor credits. Ineligible-school/unaccredited-home-study route may qualify by ACT 29 or SAT 1340 before completion; a separately described retroactive route uses earlier qualifying test scores and 3.3 college HOPE GPA at 30 semester/45 quarter hours. ACT equivalence is reviewed annually; check the 2027 posting.
notes: Calculated HOPE GPA differs from school GPA: school weighting removed, limited 0.5 AP/IB/degree-level dual-enrolment weighting restored below A; honors not weighted, no rounding, with approved advanced fine arts counted starting class of 2027.
