Private colleges require at least six credits; public institutions have no minimum credit load.

provider: Tennessee Higher Education Commission and Student Assistance Corporation
name: Tennessee HOPE Scholarship
value: Up to $2,250 per full-time semester freshman/sophomore and $2,850 junior/senior at four-year institutions or two-year institutions with on-campus housing; up to $1,600 at other two-year institutions. Summer funding available. Generally 75% of full award at 9-11 credits and 50% at 6-8; under six normally not funded, with graduation/programme exceptions. Only courses leading to the eligible associate/bachelor programme are funded.
deadline: Recurring FAFSA receipt deadlines: September 1 for fall, March 1 for spring and May 1 for summer. Official programme guidance does not label these dates with a 2027 cycle year or time zone.
apply: Complete FAFSA each year; this applies for HOPE and its GAMS supplement. Institution verifies final academic eligibility and credits funds to the school account. Monitor THEC Student Portal and college financial-aid office; homeschool applicants should request specific GAMS review if applicable.
eligibility: Tennessee resident, eligible high-school graduate enrolling within 16 months. Standard Tennessee-school path: ACT 21 or SAT 1060 before college enrolment, OR overall 3.0 GPA under the weighted Tennessee Uniform Grading Policy. Homeschool GPA is not used: ACT/SAT route or specified two dual-enrolment courses totalling six credits with 3.0 in each and cumulative dual-enrolment GPA. GED/HiSET routes require qualifying test scores plus ACT requirement. Qualified out-of-state-school exceptions include adjoining counties, military/DoD, foreign religious service and accredited boarding schools. ACT superscores/residual tests not accepted. College renewal needs 2.75 at 24/48 attempted hours, then 3.0 at 72 and later 24-hour benchmarks, or conditional 2.75-2.99 cumulative plus 3.0 term GPA/full-time attendance.
notes: Awards require eligible Tennessee institution and continued fall/spring enrolment, satisfactory academic progress and annual FAFSA. Normal five-year limit from initial postsecondary enrolment; documented disability may qualify for extension. Changing enrolment load or leaving school can affect eligibility; one academic regain opportunity at a later benchmark.

provider: Tennessee Higher Education Commission and Student Assistance Corporation
name: General Assembly Merit Scholarship (HOPE supplement)
value: Up to $500 per semester, including summer, in addition to HOPE while continuing HOPE eligibility. Institution disburses the scholarship to the school account; normal five-year limit from initial enrolment applies.
deadline: Recurring FAFSA receipt deadlines: September 1 for fall, March 1 for spring and May 1 for summer. Official programme guidance does not label these dates with a 2027 cycle year or time zone.
apply: Complete FAFSA each year; this applies for HOPE and its GAMS supplement. Institution verifies final academic eligibility and credits funds to the school account. Monitor THEC Student Portal and college financial-aid office; homeschool applicants should request specific GAMS review if applicable.
eligibility: Must qualify for Tennessee HOPE. Tennessee public/category I-III private-school graduates: 3.75 weighted Uniform Grading Policy GPA AND ACT 29 or SAT 1330 on an eligible single administration before college enrolment. Homeschool/noncategory school route has separate academic requirements: ACT 29/SAT 1330 plus qualifying dual-enrolment coursework, Governor's School, AP examinations or CLEP result as specified by the programme. ACT superscores/residual tests not accepted. No universal high-school GPA minimum applies across those routes.
notes: Awards require eligible Tennessee institution and continued fall/spring enrolment, satisfactory academic progress and annual FAFSA. Normal five-year limit from initial postsecondary enrolment; documented disability may qualify for extension. Changing enrolment load or leaving school can affect eligibility; one academic regain opportunity at a later benchmark.

provider: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
name: Palmetto Fellows Scholarship
value: Up to $6,700 freshman year and $7,500 subsequent eligible years toward cost of attendance after other gift aid, half fall/half spring. Normally two terms for one-year certificates, four for associates, eight for first bachelors, ten for approved five-year bachelors. Renewal requires 3.0 institutional GPA, 30 new earned credits annually and continued full-time attendance/residency/certifications. Approved STEM, accounting or education enhancements can add up to $2,500 annually starting sophomore year, normally up to $10,000 combined. Education enhancement requires a teaching-service contract.
deadline: For Class of 2027, the official student packet lists May 1 early and July 15 late application deadlines. Students must submit electronically before 11:59 p.m. on the deadline date; deadline dates falling on a weekend or holiday move to the preceding Friday. Time zone is not stated.
apply: School counselor or homeschool administrator initiates the electronic application; student submits their own form. Provide required UGP transcript/rank report, test verification and signatures. Early-route scores are accepted through April national testing; late-route scores through June, with June test scores sent directly to CHE using SAT 4313 or ACT 6326 and received by July 15. If eligible, submit the College Designation Form through the Palmetto Fellows dashboard, including for out-of-state institutions.
eligibility: South Carolina resident at graduation/enrolment, U.S. citizen or eligible lawful permanent resident, eligible school/homeschool senior enrolling full-time in eligible SC institution. Early standard route: 3.50 unrounded SC UGP GPA after junior year, SAT 1200 or CHE-equivalent ACT (current packet 25), top 6% at end of sophomore/junior year. Late uses senior-year GPA and rank from sophomore/junior/senior year. Alternate route: 4.00 UGP GPA and SAT 1400 or current ACT equivalent 31 without rank. Mid-year graduates cannot use rank. Current regulation and packet include public two-year routes; confirm each participating institution because landing page and private two-year wording conflict. Specified criminal-history, aid-default/refund and lawful-presence restrictions apply.
notes: Current May 2026 regulation updates ACT Science to optional; follow current CHE superscore instructions. Base award renewal excludes AP/CLEP/dual-enrolment and immediate post-graduation summer credits from annual 30-credit requirement. Noneducation enhancements normally require 14 approved math/science/accounting credits by end of first college year; education recipients must work one year in a South Carolina public school per year of stipend, with default provisions. Approved disability, military and gap-year exceptions exist.

provider: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
name: LIFE Scholarship
value: Up to $5,000 annually at eligible four-year institutions ($4,700 tuition plus $300 book allowance); two-year amounts based on eligible tuition/book costs, capped at $5,000. Cost-of-attendance ceiling applies with other gift aid. Normally two terms for one-year certificates, four for associates, six for approved 68-credit associates, eight for first bachelors, ten for approved five-year degrees. Renewal requires 3.0 LIFE GPA and average 30 earned credits per academic year. Approved STEM, accounting or education majors may add up to $2,500 annually starting sophomore year; education recipients sign a South Carolina public-school teaching obligation.
deadline: No separate statewide scholarship application. Submit required admission, official academic records and eligibility documents by the college financial-aid office's deadlines; mid-year graduates require additional early-graduation documents.
apply: College determines eligibility using official final high-school transcript, residency/citizenship verification and any applicable test/rank documentation. Submit required criminal-history and financial-aid default/refund certifications. No FAFSA needed solely for this merit award; other financial aid may need it. Mid-year applicants provide principal/counselor certification and early-graduation documents.
eligibility: South Carolina resident and U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident at high-school graduation and enrolment; full-time eligible degree student. Four-year freshman route requires two of three: 3.0 unrounded SC Uniform Grading Policy GPA, SAT 1100 or ACT equivalent 22, top 30% approved UGP class rank. Nonranking schools require GPA plus test route. Two-year freshman route requires 3.0 UGP GPA. Eligible SC schools/homeschool or qualified out-of-state dependent route applies; later college eligibility can be earned with LIFE GPA/credit requirements. Enhancement requires approved major and normally 14 eligible math/science/accounting credits by end of first college year; education route has separate service-contract requirements.
notes: Cannot receive this award alongside Palmetto Fellows, the other South Carolina merit scholarship or Lottery Tuition Assistance in the same academic year. Mid-year graduates cannot use class rank. Specified felony and repeated alcohol/drug offence restrictions, financial-aid default/refund restrictions and annual certifications apply. Approved disability and military exceptions exist; specialised out-of-state disability institutions need CHE approval. Funding remains subject to state rules and appropriations.

provider: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
name: South Carolina HOPE Scholarship (freshman year)
value: Up to $2,800 total, including $300 book allowance, toward cost of attendance in freshman year only, normally two terms with half paid in fall and half in spring. Combined gift aid cannot exceed cost of attendance; institutional disbursement, not a renewable four-year award.
deadline: No separate statewide scholarship application. Submit required admission, official academic records and eligibility documents by the college financial-aid office's deadlines; mid-year graduates require additional early-graduation documents.
apply: College determines eligibility using official final high-school transcript, residency/citizenship verification and any applicable test/rank documentation. Submit required criminal-history and financial-aid default/refund certifications. No FAFSA needed solely for this merit award; other financial aid may need it. Mid-year applicants provide principal/counselor certification and early-graduation documents.
eligibility: South Carolina resident and U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident at high-school graduation and college enrolment; minimum 3.0 unrounded SC Uniform Grading Policy GPA at graduation; first-time full-time degree student at eligible four-year institution who does not receive LIFE or Palmetto Fellows. Approved homeschool and qualified out-of-state dependent graduates can qualify with UGP transcript conversion as applicable; GED graduates are not eligible for initial HOPE. Normally at least 12 non-remedial/non-continuing-education credits; approved disability exceptions exist.
notes: Cannot receive this award alongside Palmetto Fellows, the other South Carolina merit scholarship or Lottery Tuition Assistance in the same academic year. Mid-year graduates cannot use class rank. Specified felony and repeated alcohol/drug offence restrictions, financial-aid default/refund restrictions and annual certifications apply. Approved disability and military exceptions exist; specialised out-of-state disability institutions need CHE approval. Funding remains subject to state rules and appropriations.

provider: Louisiana Office of Student Financial Assistance (LOSFA)
name: TOPS Opportunity, Performance and Honors Awards
value: Opportunity: institution-specific amount based on 2016-17 tuition, not a promise to cover current full tuition; Performance adds $400 annually and Honors adds $800 annually. Private LAICU amount uses weighted public-institution base. Normally up to eight semesters/twelve quarters, subject to appropriations and any late-score/application reductions. 2027-28 institution payment amounts not confirmed.
deadline: Full-award application receipt: July 1, or next business day, following one-year anniversary of high-school graduation. FAFSA priority February 1 of senior year. All initial-eligibility documentation due January 15 following final application deadline. Current testing guidance requires April national ACT/CLT deadline and March SAT deadline in graduation year to avoid reduced eligibility; later qualifying tests before August 1 normally reduce funding by one semester/two quarters. Exact 2027 testing days/time zone not stated; special military/out-of-state-return deadlines apply.
apply: Submit FAFSA for academic year immediately following graduation, or TOPS Online Application only if family finances make applicant ineligible for federal grant aid. Save receipt and match name/date-of-birth across transcript and testing records. LOSFA may request official academic records, residency affidavit and citizenship/PR documentation; homeschool registration and prior-school records need verification. Send official scores using LOSFA codes (ACT 1595, SAT 9019; select LOSFA/TOPS for CLT), monitor Student Hub and respond to requests. FAFSA renewal normally annual; initial TOPS-only applicants do not refile that form annually.
eligibility: Standard approved-school route: 19 TOPS core units with core GPA 2.50 for Opportunity, 3.25 Performance or 3.50 Honors; the 2027 graduate core allows two listed Computer Science courses instead of two same-language foreign-language units; ACT respectively prior-year Louisiana average (never below 20), 23 or 27. Opportunity threshold is set annually. Current homeschool guidance instead uses ACT 20/23/27 or specified SAT/CLT equivalents without the core/GPA route; older award pages still show higher homeschool scores. Eligible out-of-state-school route uses higher ACT scores 23/26/30 in lieu of core/GPA. U.S. citizen or permanent resident at graduation; pending prior-to-graduation permanent-residency application requires LOSFA review and cannot be paid until approved. Louisiana residency normally established through final two school years or 24-month student/parent/legal-guardian residency; qualified military exceptions exist. Confirm graduation-year core and test rules with LOSFA.
notes: Only eligible Louisiana institutions. ACT superscores not accepted. Annual full-time/continuous enrolment and normally 24 earned academic-year credits required; all college coursework, including dual enrolment, affects GPA. Opportunity renewal needs 2.30 at 24-47 hours then 2.50; Performance/Honors/Excellence need 3.00 at annual review, with intermediate steady-progress conditions. Higher awards can revert permanently to Opportunity after GPA shortfall. GPA suspension can be restored within allowed period; approved medical/military exceptions concern enrolment/credits. National Guard has separate tuition-exemption/book benefits and larger education stipends; check award-specific rules. Remaining eligibility may fund graduate/professional study under enrolment rule, not a second bachelor degree.

provider: Louisiana Office of Student Financial Assistance (LOSFA)
name: TOPS Excellence Award
value: Eligible public institution: actual tuition/fees reported through Board of Regents survey, capped at $12,000 annually; eligible private LAICU institution: actual tuition/fees capped at $8,500 annually. Normally up to eight semesters/twelve quarters, subject to appropriations and late-score/application reductions. Institution receives payment directly.
deadline: Full-award application receipt: July 1, or next business day, following one-year anniversary of high-school graduation. FAFSA priority February 1 of senior year. All initial-eligibility documentation due January 15 following final application deadline. Current testing guidance requires April national ACT/CLT deadline and March SAT deadline in graduation year to avoid reduced eligibility; later qualifying tests before August 1 normally reduce funding by one semester/two quarters. Exact 2027 testing days/time zone not stated; special military/out-of-state-return deadlines apply.
apply: Submit FAFSA for academic year immediately following graduation, or TOPS Online Application only if family finances make applicant ineligible for federal grant aid. Save receipt and match name/date-of-birth across transcript and testing records. LOSFA may request official academic records, residency affidavit and citizenship/PR documentation; homeschool registration and prior-school records need verification. Send official scores using LOSFA codes (ACT 1595, SAT 9019; select LOSFA/TOPS for CLT), monitor Student Hub and respond to requests. FAFSA renewal normally annual; initial TOPS-only applicants do not refile that form annually.
eligibility: Standard approved-school route: 19 TOPS core units, minimum 3.50 TOPS core GPA and ACT 31; the 2027 graduate core allows two listed Computer Science courses instead of two same-language foreign-language units. Qualified out-of-state-school route uses ACT 34 in lieu of core/GPA; approved homeschool route uses ACT 31 or specified SAT/CLT equivalents. First-time full-time enrolment at eligible Louisiana institution by first semester following one-year graduation anniversary. U.S. citizen or permanent resident at graduation; pending prior-to-graduation permanent-residency application requires LOSFA review and cannot be paid until approved. Louisiana residency normally established through final two school years or 24-month student/parent/legal-guardian residency; qualified military exceptions exist. Confirm graduation-year core and test rules with LOSFA.
notes: Only eligible Louisiana institutions. ACT superscores not accepted. Annual full-time/continuous enrolment and normally 24 earned academic-year credits required; all college coursework, including dual enrolment, affects GPA. Opportunity renewal needs 2.30 at 24-47 hours then 2.50; Performance/Honors/Excellence need 3.00 at annual review, with intermediate steady-progress conditions. Higher awards can revert permanently to Opportunity after GPA shortfall. GPA suspension can be restored within allowed period; approved medical/military exceptions concern enrolment/credits. National Guard has separate tuition-exemption/book benefits and larger education stipends; check award-specific rules. Remaining eligibility may fund graduate/professional study under enrolment rule, not a second bachelor degree.

name: Kentucky Educational Excellence Scholarship (KEES)
value: Each qualifying high-school year earns $187 at 2.75 GPA to $500 at 4.00 toward each college year; earned annual base amounts accumulate. Highest pregraduation ACT/SAT bonus up to $500; free/reduced-lunch eligible students can add $200-$300 per qualifying AP/IB/Cambridge examination, with no examination-count cap. Half-time college enrolment minimum; part-time amounts adjusted. Award expires at eight funded semesters, five years after graduation or bachelor degree, whichever first. Separate comprehensive-transition programme awards for students with intellectual disabilities are $250/$500 per term based on load, up to eight terms.
deadline: No separate ordinary college scholarship application. Optional workforce reimbursement for July 2026-June 2027 expenses requires postmark by June 1, 2027; 2027-28 reimbursement deadline not published in current guidance.
apply: No separate application for ordinary college route: school reports grades, test results and eligibility; check MyKHEAA records and college financial-aid office. Approved workforce reimbursement instead requires Pathway Selection Form, request form and clear itemised receipts after eligible expenses are paid.
eligibility: Kentucky resident, U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident; not a convicted felon. Certified-school GPA route needs approved curriculum and at least 2.75 in an award-earning year beginning 2026-27. Kentucky homeschool/noncertified-school graduates and qualifying GED recipients (age 18-23) can earn a score-only award, without the school GPA route. Certain Kentucky-resident military dependents, exchange/Page School students and approved programmes outside Kentucky qualify.
notes: Full renewal after first college year needs 2.50 cumulative GPA. Later full renewal requires 3.00 OR 2.50-2.99 plus certified on-track graduation progress. A 50% award may apply at 2.50-2.99 off track with prior full-time enrolment; below 2.50 loses award until eligible at a later spring review. Summer grades cannot repair preceding spring determination. Comprehensive-transition awards have separate renewal exception. Approved workforce/apprenticeship/proprietary/KCTCS and art/design reimbursement routes exist; ordinary out-of-state college use requires Academic Common Market approval.

name: Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 lifetime tuition benefit, paid per credit up to 15 credits each semester: $40 lower/$60 upper division at NSHE community colleges, $60 Nevada State University, $80 other eligible institutions. Remedial/graduate courses excluded; student pays uncovered costs. Normally six years after high-school graduation, with military/service/disability extensions. Institution credits account; summer often requires upfront payment and later reimbursement.
deadline: No separate traditional-school application deadline; school reports after graduation and student acknowledges award. Nontraditional forms refer to Board of Regents graduation-year limitations without stating a 2027 dated deadline.
apply: Traditional school reports eligible students; award packet normally mailed July/August, then student must acknowledge award online and complete citizenship affidavit. Enrol in recognised eligible degree/certificate programme with 12 university/state-college or nine community-college credits. Homeschool/out-of-state applicants use linked form with signed application, official sealed transcript if applicable, official ACT/SAT results, residency/dependency documents and homeschool district-waiver documentation as applicable.
eligibility: Traditional Nevada public/private/charter graduate: 3.25 weighted or unweighted GPA OR SAT 1070/ACT 21, specified 4 English/4 math (Algebra II or higher)/3 science/3 history, and at least two years Nevada residency. Homeschool and out-of-state-school graduates have separate test, school-record and dependent-residency rules in linked forms; confirm those routes directly. U.S. citizenship is not universally required, but applicant must truthfully complete citizenship/immigration affidavit during award acknowledgement.
notes: Only eligible Nevada institutions; institutional award timing varies. Continued eligibility requires 2.75 semester GPA, satisfactory progress and completing required 12/9 credits. Reinstatement normally automatic after regaining requirements; programme expiration still applies. Current linked nontraditional forms bear October 2019 dates, despite 2024 filenames, and need confirmation for the applicant's graduation year.

provider: West Virginia Higher Education Policy Commission
name: PROMISE Scholarship
value: Up to $5,500 per year or eligible tuition/mandatory fees, whichever less; maximum determined annually and funding contingent on state appropriations. Institution receives payment for degree-pursuant undergraduate coursework. Up to eight bachelor semesters or four associate semesters; normally must use within six years after award, with military extension. Completion of degree ends eligibility. Renewal normally 2.75 overall college GPA and 30 earned credits per two-semester academic year (15 for one semester), continuous full-time enrolment, with final-year exceptions.
deadline: Class of 2027: Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA open October 1, 2026; both must meet submission/processing conditions by March 1, 2027. Last qualifying SAT administration is June 2027; last qualifying national ACT is July 2027. No time zone stated.
apply: Create WVSAM account, verify email, submit Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA by March 1, 2027, even if qualifying grades/scores are still pending. Send individual official test administrations (ACT code 4539, SAT 3456) and monitor matching/status. Public-school academic records generally supplied through school system; private-school final records and special homeschool/commuter/military forms require school/applicant verification. Scholars do not reapply annually; annual FAFSA encouraged for other aid.
eligibility: Class of 2027: overall high-school GPA at least 3.0/B under approved school policy; separate core GPA requirement removed. ACT composite 21 on English/reading/math or SAT 1080; superscores accepted beginning 2027-28, without mixing ACT/SAT formats. U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen. Student AND FAFSA parent/legal guardian normally need 12 consecutive months WV residency before deadline; at least half high-school credits completed at qualifying WV school and eligible graduation route. Qualified homeschool/Hope-IIP, daily out-of-state commuter, military and approved alternative-education routes require additional documents. First-time full-time initial award normally within two years of graduation, with specified exceptions.
notes: Only eligible WV public/private two- or four-year institutions; total aid cannot exceed cost of attendance. Late applicants may receive spring funding only if funds remain. All college grades, including dual enrolment and credits the college does not accept, affect cumulative GPA; prematriculation credits cannot meet renewal credit minimum. Summer courses paid by student may repair renewal. One Second Chance renewal opportunity; recovery terms count toward maximum duration. Final academic year has enrolment/renewal exceptions.

provider: Mississippi Office of Student Financial Aid
name: Mississippi Eminent Scholars Grant (MESG)
value: Up to $2,500 per academic year, capped at tuition/mandatory fees; divided among fall/spring terms and paid to institution. Up to eight semesters/twelve trimesters or required degree/certificate completion, whichever first. Renewal normally requires 3.50 cumulative college GPA and continuous full-time completion.
deadline: Mississippi State University official 2027-28 calendar confirms MAAPP application deadline September 15, 2027. State rules require supporting documents by October 15 following the application deadline; that stage is published as a recurring rule, without a 2027 year/time zone. Apply annually and monitor state requests.
apply: Submit annual MAAPP, verify account/email and monitor requests. New applicants and certain students returning after interruption supply two approved residency documents (e.g. Mississippi driver licence and FAFSA or approved state-tax/homestead/voter/vehicle records), plus official academic/test documentation and signed and notarized homeschool transcript including all courses and an unweighted seven-semester GPA on a 4.0 scale where applicable. Institution supplies enrolment/renewal grades; FAFSA alone does not apply for state aid.
eligibility: Mississippi legal resident, normally one year before high-school/homeschool completion. Standard school route: 3.50 cumulative school-policy GPA AND ACT 29/SAT equivalent 1330, or qualifying National Merit finalist/semifinalist designation. ACT superscores accepted. Linked current regulation provides a grades 9-12 homeschool route based on ACT/SAT without stated high-school GPA; overview instead says 3.50 and signed transcript for homeschool. Initial application within three school years after graduation; first-time college route and limited prior out-of-state credit route have separate college-GPA conditions. Cannot owe state/federal aid refund or be in default; institution general aid requirements apply.
notes: Eligible Mississippi nonprofit public/private institutions only; first certificate/associate/bachelor pathway. Continuous fall/spring full-time completion normally 12 credits each semester; summer not funded. Awards paid to institution, first toward tuition, contingent on appropriations and cost-of-attendance limits. Only one state undergraduate grant per term, choosing larger eligible award, and maximum combined eight semesters. GPA/enrolment loss has specified regain/appeal procedures; institution corrections have fall October 15 and spring March 15 verification deadlines.

provider: Mississippi Office of Student Financial Aid
name: Mississippi Tuition Assistance Grant (MTAG)
value: Up to $500 annually freshman/sophomore or $1,000 junior/senior, also limited by gap between maximum Pell and applicant Pell eligibility. Normally eight semesters/twelve trimesters or required degree/certificate completion, whichever first. Renewal normally 2.50 cumulative college GPA; certificate routes use institutional satisfactory-progress standards.
deadline: Mississippi State University official 2027-28 calendar confirms MAAPP application deadline September 15, 2027. State rules require supporting documents by October 15 following the application deadline; that stage is published as a recurring rule, without a 2027 year/time zone. Apply annually and monitor state requests.
apply: Submit annual MAAPP, verify account/email and monitor requests. New applicants and certain students returning after interruption supply two approved residency documents (e.g. Mississippi driver licence and FAFSA or approved state-tax/homestead/voter/vehicle records), plus official academic/test documentation and signed and notarized homeschool transcript including all courses and an unweighted seven-semester GPA on a 4.0 scale where applicable. Institution supplies enrolment/renewal grades; FAFSA alone does not apply for state aid. FAFSA is the usual financial determination. The sponsor FAQ and linked regulation permit a Statement of Certification as an alternative for students/parents who believe they will not qualify for the Federal Pell Grant; read and complete the certification statements in MAAPP carefully.
eligibility: Mississippi legal resident, normally one year before application. Standard school route 2.50 cumulative GPA plus ACT 15/SAT equivalent; ACT superscores accepted. Home education and high-school-equivalency routes have score/document alternatives without universal school GPA; 12 completed college hours with 2.50 college GPA can establish eligibility without original school score/GPA. Vocational/technical community-college certificate/applied-associate route need not take ACT unless college requires. Must be ineligible for maximum Pell; cannot be in aid default or owe grant repayment; institution general aid conditions apply.
notes: Eligible Mississippi nonprofit public/private institutions only; first certificate/associate/bachelor pathway. Continuous fall/spring full-time completion normally 12 credits each semester; summer not funded. Awards paid to institution, first toward tuition, contingent on appropriations and cost-of-attendance limits. Only one state undergraduate grant per term, choosing larger eligible award, and maximum combined eight semesters. GPA/enrolment loss has specified regain/appeal procedures; institution corrections have fall October 15 and spring March 15 verification deadlines.

name: Arkansas Academic Challenge Scholarship
value: Ongoing rates beginning 2025-26: four-year institution $2,000 year one, $4,000 years two/three, $5,000 year four; two-year institution $2,000 year one and $3,000 year two. Need-based Challenge PLUS can increase total to $2,500 per semester based on FAFSA SAI. Final-year, nontraditional and graduate funding have load rules; current sources disagree on some fifth-semester two-year/stacked allocations. Normally eight payments, bachelor completion or 120 credits, with approved longer-degree exception.
deadline: Annual application July 1; current guidance does not label a 2027 cycle year/time zone. Qualifying ACT can be taken through national July administration. Summer opt-in recurring June 1; transfers/holds recurring October 1 fall or February 1 spring.
apply: Create SAMS account and apply, complete FAFSA even if no financial need, monitor academic/test matching and requests, accept award and keep institution/contact records current. No annual scholarship reapplication for renewal. Programme has separate hold, transfer, summer opt-in and graduate-use forms; follow deadlines in SAMS notices.
eligibility: Arkansas resident for 12 months before enrolment and U.S. citizen/lawful permanent resident; accepted in approved degree/certificate/nursing programme, no prior bachelor or 120 credits. Traditional route: Diploma of Merit, OR GPA below 3.00/equivalent plus ACT 19/SAT 990/Accuplacer average 246, OR GPA 3.00+ plus test score on record without score minimum. Later first-year college route can use 27 credits with 2.50 GPA. Nontraditional applicants have college-GPA or test/GPA routes, but overview and detailed section differ for the no-college-credit GPA-only route. ACT official composites/superscores accepted; ADHE cannot manually remove science. Aid refund/loan-limit, incarceration, Selective Service and drug-free restrictions apply.
notes: Traditional load normally 12 first fall then 15 each semester, renewal 2.50 GPA and 27 first-year/30 later annual credits. Current recipient sheet allows fourth-year payment at six or more credits without reduction, conflicting with broader proration guidance; confirm load exceptions. Nontraditional six-to-14-credit funding may be prorated. One eligible institution or approved consortium; continuous enrolment and approved holds up to four semesters. Summer paid terms consume eligibility and have additional earned-credit duties; early graduates may use limited remaining senior payments for approved graduate study.

name: Governor's Distinguished Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 annually for four years/eight semester payments toward institution-billed tuition, mandatory fees, room and board. Combined Governor's Distinguished plus Academic Challenge funding cannot exceed $10,000 annually; it is not $10,000 plus the Challenge award. Institution receives nonrefundable funding; uncovered cost and cost-of-attendance/load limits can reduce it.
deadline: Annual application March 1; qualifying scores through national February ACT testing deadline. Current guidance does not provide an explicit 2027 dated schedule/time zone. Summer opt-in recurring June 1; transfers/holds recurring October 1 fall or February 1 spring.
apply: Apply in SAMS and normally complete FAFSA, monitor official academic/test matching and accept award. If a qualifying February test score arrives after an earlier SAMS application, submit updated scholarship application before deadline to notify ADHE. Students or parents with EAD should contact ADHE about alternate eligibility and FAFSA exemption. No yearly scholarship reapplication for renewal; summer/hold/graduate-use forms separate.
eligibility: Arkansas resident for 12 months; graduating senior with 3.50 cumulative GPA AND official ACT composite/superscore 32 or SAT 1410 on single administration. U.S. citizen/permanent resident OR student/parent holding Employment Authorization Document; EAD route exempt from FAFSA. First fall normally 12 credits, then 15 each semester, at one approved institution or approved consortium. ADHE cannot manually add/remove ACT science. Non-distinguished Governor's Scholars has separate Diploma of Distinction/associate routes and is not automatically this $10,000 award.
notes: Renewal normally 3.25 cumulative GPA, 27 first-year then 30 annual credits, institutional satisfactory progress and drug-free certification. Fourth-year load can be prorated at six-to-eight (50%) or nine-to-14 (75%) credits. Combined funding allocation tables disagree on first-year split while agreeing total cap; confirm institution breakdown. Approved holds up to four semesters. Early bachelor graduates may use at most remaining senior-year payments for approved graduate/professional programme, with enrolment/document requirements and limited eligible out-of-state professional agreements.

name: New Mexico Legislative Lottery Scholarship
value: 100% of tuition at New Mexico public colleges and universities, up to seven semesters (three at community colleges). The Opportunity Scholarship can cover the first qualifying semester and course fees.
deadline: No separate scholarship application. Normally establish full-time college eligibility within 16 months after qualifying high-school/HSE/homeschool completion; follow institutional admission/enrolment deadlines. Disability documentation has separate preterm timing; ask financial-aid office.
apply: No separate scholarship application or FAFSA required. Enrol/register at eligible New Mexico public institution and notify financial-aid adviser that first full-time semester establishes Lottery eligibility. College determines qualification and credits award. Disability accommodation requires student-services documentation and timely notice before term.
eligibility: New Mexico resident (normally 12 consecutive months) with qualifying New Mexico high-school graduation, HSE while resident or registered homeschool completion; first bachelor not yet earned. Eligible out-of-state members of a Nation/Tribe/Pueblo wholly or partly in New Mexico can qualify with membership proof. Noncitizens may qualify through nondiscrimination waiver after at least one year New Mexico high-school attendance and qualifying NM graduation/HSE. Establish and maintain 2.50 college GPA, full-time 15 credits four-year or 12 community college within 16 months and continuous fall/spring enrolment, with disability/approved interruption exceptions.
notes: Tuition only at eligible participating New Mexico public institutions, not private/out-of-state colleges. Lottery starts after qualifying first semester; bridge/Opportunity aid may fund that term and course-specific fees. Up to seven bachelor-funded semesters or first bachelor completion, three community-college semesters; disability exceptions may extend. Summer optional. Withdrawal/credit shortfall needs prompt institutional review; approved leave may preserve eligibility.

provider: Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education
name: Oklahoma Rising Scholars Award (formerly Academic Scholars Program)
value: Fall 2026 entry table lists automatic-qualifier amounts $24,000 research universities, $13,000 regional and $12,500 two-year, plus public-institution tuition waiver. 2027-entry amounts are not published; table does not clearly label payment period for these new automatic amounts. Institutional nominee table explicitly $4,000/$3,200/$3,000 per year respectively. Normally eight semesters; institution disbursement and cost-of-attendance reduction apply.
deadline: No initial application deadline or 2027 dated schedule published on programme/FAQ pages. Must accept as first-time student at Oklahoma institution in fall immediately after high-school graduation. Institutional nomination and optional summer funding have separate procedures/deadlines.
apply: Automatic qualifiers use linked online application; State Regents verify supporting documentation and may request more by email. Other applicants contact college about institutional nomination. College coordinator certifies enrolment, annual GPA/credits and payment. Summer requires separate application and 24 earned fall/spring credits; transfer, leave and graduate-transfer forms available. Full current application-form fields were not readable in public Smartsheet tool output.
eligibility: Oklahoma resident automatic route: National Merit Scholar/Finalist or U.S. Presidential Scholar, or 99.5-percentile ACT/SAT. Published fall 2026 score is ACT 103 sum of English/math/reading or SAT 1560; these are not confirmed for 2027. Institutions may nominate under separate academic criteria, which require college/programme review. Concurrent high-school students cannot receive programme funding until high-school completion.
notes: Renewal requires 3.25 cumulative/retention GPA and normally 12 credits each fall/spring, 24 earned annually. Funded summer raises annual earned-credit requirement to 30 (six-to-11 summer credits) or 36 (12+); consumes half/full semester. Deficiency generally has one academic year to remedy, with unpaid deficiency terms counting against duration. Approved leave/study-abroad/graduate-transition routes have written notice and limits. Institutional nominees have first-year and transfer restrictions; out-of-state attendance normally consumes eligibility without funding.

provider: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
name: Bright Flight (Missouri Higher Education Academic Scholarship)
value: Published 2026-graduate estimates: $3,000 annually for ACT 32+ or SAT math 800/reading 800; $1,000 for ACT 30-31 or SAT math 800/reading 790-799. These are not confirmed 2027 cutoffs or awards. Statutory annual maxima $3,000/$1,000; divided fall/spring, no summer. Up to ten semesters or first bachelor, subject to appropriation.
deadline: No scholarship application. Earn qualifying score by June testing immediately after graduation; July does not qualify. Exact 2027 qualifying test dates/cutoffs are not published. Respond by any individually assigned supplemental-document deadline.
apply: Automatic consideration from official ACT/SAT records and approved Missouri college choices; no FAFSA required. ACT superscores must be sent separately using code 2379 and testing-service fee. Allow six-to-eight weeks for scores to reach state; monitor Student Portal and correct conflicting residency/citizenship/college information. GED/HiSet applicants supply certificate copy. College certifies each term and disburses award.
eligibility: Missouri resident and U.S. citizen/permanent resident, qualifying top-five-percent ACT/SAT score on national or approved special test (not residual); homeschool and GED/HiSet routes included. First-time full-time attendance at participating Missouri institution in academic year immediately after school completion, normally 12 credits or six with qualifying disability. Theology/divinity degree or certificate excluded. Current 2027 score cutoffs not published.
notes: Renewal normally cumulative college GPA 2.50 and institutional satisfactory progress; GPA requirement waived first academic year receiving payment. Receive at least one funded semester every academic year. Notify state of transfer. Approved exchange/nonprofit-government/medical deferral normally up to 27 months; military deferral has separate return timing. Only participating Missouri institutions.

provider: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction and North Dakota University System
name: North Dakota Scholarship
value: $750 per semester, up to $6,000, usable at approved North Dakota colleges, universities, professional schools and registered apprenticeship programs within six years of graduation.
deadline: Class of 2027 official application portal: opens January 4, 2027; submit by June 4, 2027. Later applications are not guaranteed processing for fall 2027 payment. School Choice Ready report has separate recurring June 30 deadline; confirm school submission. No time zone stated.
apply: Create/use North Dakota Login and complete Class of 2027 application. School submits Choice Ready eligibility report; nonpublic schools use verification form. Homeschool applicants supply notices of intent for home-education years, notarised grades 9-12 transcript and verification, official test and dual-enrolment records. Tests must be taken before graduation; send later-than-March ACT results to NDDPI code 2927. No annual reapplication after award; institution certifies renewal.
eligibility: North Dakota resident at graduation with ND high-school diploma, including documented homeschool route. Essential Skills: 3.00 overall unweighted GPA, civics test 70%+, nine weeks career education/counselling, four-year rolling plan and four of eight additional indicators. Also complete two of three pathways: Post-Secondary Ready (ACT 24/SAT 1180 plus two approved academic indicators), Workforce Ready (required CTE/language coursework, ACT 24/SAT 1180 or WorkKeys all three scores 5+, plus two workforce indicators), Military Ready (ASVAB 50+, or 31+ with basic training within 90 days after graduation, required PE plus two indicators). ACT superscores allowed. Same dual course cannot satisfy both pathway indicators.
notes: Maximum combined $6,000 across ND scholarship programmes, $750 semester/$500 quarter, within six academic years of graduation. Approved ND institutions/professional/apprenticeship programmes only. Renew full time under institution definition and cumulative college GPA 2.75 checked each term; one below-GPA term exception, second loses eligibility. Earned-credit thresholds for semester payments three through eight: 24, 39, 54, 69, 84, 99. First two payments require full time. Approved graduate use/deferment can apply.

name: South Dakota Opportunity Scholarship
value: Up to $7,500 total: $1,500 annually first three years, $3,000 fourth year, paid half each fall/spring. Up to eight consecutive fall/spring terms or first bachelor, whichever first. Renewal requires cumulative college GPA 3.00 (checked after second term then every term), persistence and 30/60/90 earned credits before sophomore/junior/senior payments. One GPA reinstatement possible; lost time not extended.
deadline: Current Board of Regents timeline and September 2026 handout: first-time fall September 1 (preferred June 1), spring January 15 (preferred November 1), without cycle years/time zone. Programme overview instead says spring January 1 (preferred September 1); confirm spring timing. In-state transfer overview: fall September 20, spring February 15; out-of-state return fall September 1, spring January 15. No explicit 2027 dated schedule published.
apply: Complete SD Opportunity Scholarship Application in SDBOR Scholarship Portal, using public-university email if already dual-enrolled/enrolled, otherwise create manual account. Same application covers new and transfer students. Current handout says high-school transcript verified through admissions, with no additional transcript submission. Ensure official scores and class-of-2027 curriculum/endorsement are reflected in institutional review; homeschool transcript has separate legal requirements. No annual reapplication normally.
eligibility: South Dakota resident at high-school graduation; enter eligible SD institution within five years, or qualifying military-release extension. Option 1: ACT composite/superscore 24+ or SAT 1180+, 3.00 unweighted GPA and Advanced Honors Endorsement/approved curriculum with final grades C+. Class of 2027 requires specific subject subcategories. Option 2: ACT 28+ with English 18, reading 21, math 22 and science 24 subscores, or Board of Regents SAT equivalent 1310+; no GPA/curriculum requirement. Law and official 2027 guide specify ACT subscores even though overview/handout omit them. Tests before college; separate alternative-instruction route.
notes: Only participating South Dakota institutions. Class-of-2027 curriculum: four English, four maths through advanced maths, four science (three labs), three social studies, two same-language/approved CTE combined units, fine arts, economics/personal finance, PE and health, with specific subcategories. Each course satisfies one subcategory; approved equivalent dual credit possible. Out-of-state college return within two years can receive partial award if initial and continuing standards met while away. Remedial/repeated credits do not satisfy benchmarks. No obligation to live/work in South Dakota after graduation.

name: Hathaway Scholarship
value: Per full-time semester for courses beginning July 1, 2026 onward: Honors $2,360, Performance $1,770, Opportunity/Provisional $1,180. Normally eight full-time semesters/96 credits within six years after starting; Provisional first four at WY community college with qualifying four-semester extension. Six-to-11-credit awards prorated. Need supplement separate and requires FAFSA; current university page has conflicting old/new supplement limits.
deadline: Current state guidance allows initiation within four years after high-school/HSEC graduation, or before age 21 for homeschool; military/religious-service exceptions. Apply through chosen Wyoming institution before courses begin; college-specific 2027 application/material deadlines are not published in statewide guidance. Scores accepted through start of courses.
apply: Apply through selected Wyoming college and send official final transcript/coursework and qualifying test scores; institution determines award. UW reviews new admission applicants automatically but requires Hathaway Eligibility Verification Form in WyoRecords checklist and all final/college transcripts. Community colleges have their own procedures. Transfers request separate Hathaway Transfer Transcript after grades post. FAFSA required only for optional need supplement.
eligibility: Wyoming resident as determined by institution; U.S. citizen or permanent resident eligible under Title IV. Standard school tiers: Honors 3.50 Hathaway GPA/ACT 25, Performance 3.00/21, Opportunity 2.50/19, Provisional 2.50/17 or WorkKeys 12, plus tier-specific Success Curriculum. AP/IB/college courses weighted; ACT superscores and approved equivalent exams allowed. Homeschool route uses curriculum/test without universal school GPA; HSEC uses qualifying GED/TASC/HiSet and entrance test instead. Selective Service, aid refund/default and incarceration/felony restrictions apply, with appeal rules.
notes: Only Wyoming community colleges/UW. Provisional starts community college; associate completion can allow remaining UW payments, certificate completion has specified extension. Renewal college GPA 2.25 Opportunity/Provisional, 2.50 Honors/Performance; complete at least six nonremedial credits part time or 12 full time and attend fall/spring continuously. Higher tier may temporarily receive Opportunity at 2.25. Unpaid recovery terms count within six-year limit; summer consumes funded eligibility, does not replace required fall/spring continuity. Graduate use possible with remaining eligibility.

name: MUS Honor Scholarship
value: Four-year renewable tuition waiver at an eligible Montana campus (average value about $5,000 a year at a 4-year campus); does not cover mandatory or class fees. Up to 200 awarded annually.
deadline: Applications open December 1, 2026. Complete application, college acceptance, score proof, official seventh-semester transcript and signed certification by March 15, 2027. Take ACT/SAT by February 2027; superscores may include only tests by then. School submits eligible GPA rankings by annual March 15 deadline. No time zone stated.
apply: Apply to and be accepted at eligible Montana campus, then complete AwardMontana online application. Upload acceptance letter/email, official seventh-semester transcript covering freshman through first senior semester, ACT/SAT proof and counselor-signed Rigorous Core/IB/Attendance Certification. Middle-school transcript required if counting Algebra I from middle school; other courses must appear on high-school transcript. Accept/decline promptly if offered.
eligibility: Montana resident/U.S. citizen applying in graduation year, normally three full-time years at Montana Board-accredited high school including senior year. Narrow military-parent exception permits prior out-of-state accredited schooling with Montana senior year and documented parent residency/support. Seventh-semester GPA 3.40+ using school weighting consistently; complete Rigorous Core or IB diploma by graduation. Selection combines within-school GPA rank points (rounded tenth) and ACT/SAT equivalent, with ACT superscores accepted by February 2027. Accepted eligible campus required; minimums do not guarantee award.
notes: Tuition waiver only, not mandatory/class fees, at eligible MUS/listed community campuses. Funding and target of 200 contingent on budget. Start within nine months after graduation; renew maximum eight continuous fall/spring semesters with full-time 12+ credits, annual cumulative GPA 3.40, 30/60/90 earned credits after two/four/six semesters and conduct compliance. Eligible-campus transfer requires notification; summer waiver at campus discretion, with appeal for beyond-control GPA/credit circumstances.

name: Alaska Performance Scholarship (APS)
value: Level 1 up to $7,000 per year, Level 2 up to $5,250, Level 3 up to $3,500; up to $28,000 total, usable for up to eight full-time semester equivalents within eight years of high-school graduation. Half-time awards are prorated.
deadline: Recurring policy: FAFSA or APS Alternative Application priority deadline June 30 before the academic year of use. Private/homeschool eligibility form and supporting records due July 15 for the upcoming award year. Qualifying tests must be before June 30 of graduation year. Notify the institution before its enrollment-certification deadline. No separate 2027 calendar or timezone is claimed.
apply: Complete FAFSA annually naming eligible Alaska institution, or APS Alternative Application for non-Title IV institution. Students without SSN may submit alternative to ACPE even for Title IV school, identifying institution/student ID. School reports final eligibility; create student-owned ASAP account to monitor. Independently homeschooled/private students also submit signed Eligibility Determination Application, curriculum checklist, official transcript/proof coursework and optional official test report for higher level.
eligibility: Alaska resident (physically present at least 30 days with intent to remain indefinitely) graduating from Alaska public/private/homeschool diploma programme, not GED or out-of-state high school. Complete approved rigorous curriculum option AND either GPA or score: Level 1 GPA 3.50 OR ACT 25/SAT 1210/WorkKeys 18 (each 6+); Level 2 GPA 3.00 OR 23/1130/15 (each 5+); Level 3 GPA 2.50 OR 21/1060/12 (each 4+). Current rules apply Class of 2024 onward; earlier graduates differ. Eligible degree/certificate and half-time minimum; other non-loan aid must leave at least $500 qualifying cost.
notes: Annual maxima $7,000/$5,250/$3,500; up to eight full-time semester equivalents within eight years after graduation, paid to participating Alaska provider. Covers eligible remaining attendance costs, not necessarily full amount; part-time prorated. Renew institutional progress and cumulative college GPA 2.50, first-year earned credits 24 full time/12 half time, later 30/15; graduate/credit-certificate and clock-hour routes have separate standards. Step-Up may increase tier after specified consecutive 15-credit semesters/10-credit quarters or qualifying certificates and college GPA. No SAI need test, but other non-loan aid reduces unmet costs.

name: John and Abigail Adams Scholarship
value: Credit toward required tuition for state-supported undergraduate courses, excluding fees/room/board; maximum eight nonsummer semesters within six years after high-school graduation. Campus-specific 2027-28 amounts are not confirmed. Programme overview lists UMass dollar credits, while August 2026 guideline excludes institutions retaining resident tuition, so confirm eligible-campus coverage with financial-aid office.
deadline: No scholarship application; eligible students notified in fall of senior year. Submit eligibility letter and annual FAFSA or MASFA to college under institutional financial-aid deadlines. No separate statewide 2027 scholarship deadline published.
apply: State identifies qualifying first-time MCAS scores and sends eligibility letters through school/district. Provide letter/documentation to accepted eligible Massachusetts public college, complete FAFSA annually or MASFA if FAFSA-ineligible, and fulfil aid verification. No separate merit scholarship application; transfer activation needs prior cumulative college GPA 3.00.
eligibility: Graduate from/under auspices of Massachusetts public high school, not GED, with first-attempt next-generation MCAS ELA/math/science total in district top 25%. One subject at Advanced-equivalent minimum (ELA 501, maths 504, science 522), other two Proficient-equivalent (ELA 472, maths 486, science 491). Massachusetts physical residency one year before enrolled term plus U.S. citizen/PR/Title IV eligible noncitizen, or approved tuition-equity status. Accepted full-time 12+ credit state-supported undergraduate programme, no prior bachelor, no aid default/refund, institutional progress.
notes: Non-need merit award, though annual FAFSA/MASFA required. Renewal cumulative GPA 3.00 checked each spring; falling below permanently forfeits scholarship under current guideline. Cannot combine other tuition credits. Current 2026-27 guideline and public overview differ on eligible campus/value scope; 2027-28 terms need confirmation. Retroactive credit only within academic year eligibility is documented, not prior fiscal years.

name: Valedictorian Program Tuition Waiver
value: Waiver equal to 100% of credited tuition at an eligible Massachusetts public institution; fees and other costs are separate. Institution determines additional award criteria and administration. Published statewide guidance does not establish a uniform renewal duration or 2027 campus tuition value.
deadline: Contact the college financial aid office for deadlines
apply: Contact the chosen public institution financial aid office for its Valedictorian tuition-waiver process and required proof of designation. File the current-year FAFSA or MASFA and provide residency/status and other eligibility documentation.
eligibility: Designated as valedictorian by a Massachusetts public or private high school; enroll in a degree program at a Massachusetts public institution and meet its criteria; U.S. citizen, permanent resident, Title IV eligible non-citizen, or approved tuition equity status with one year of Massachusetts residency.
notes: The 2026-27 statewide tuition-waiver guidelines confirm eligibility and tuition coverage. Individual colleges determine further award criteria and procedures; confirm renewal, duration and deadlines with the institution.

provider: New York State Higher Education Services Corporation (HESC)
name: NYS Scholarships for Academic Excellence
value: $1,500 or $500 annually, subject to appropriations. Up to two years for an associate degree, four for a bachelor’s, or five in an approved five-year program. Full-time eligible New York college attendance and satisfactory academic progress required; cumulative C average after two full years of state-aid payments.
deadline: High schools must submit 2027 nominations through SEDMON by February 26, 2027; students meet earlier school deadlines. Schools publish selection criteria by September 30, 2026. A declined award may be reassigned under the bulletin rules by April 15, 2027. Begin eligible college study in fall 2027 unless an advance one-year delay is approved. No time zone stated.
apply: Ask your high school about its nomination process; students do not self-nominate. School submits nominees, personal contact details and academic documentation through SEDMON. After nomination, follow HESC acceptance/payment instructions and file annual FAFSA and TAP application, or applicable NYS DREAM Act application.
eligibility: Graduate from an eligible New York high school in June 2027 and attend an approved New York college full time. Standard route requires 12 months of New York residency and U.S. citizenship or eligible noncitizen status; qualifying NYS DREAM Act applicants can include non-New York residents under its school-attendance and status rules. School selects using prescribed weighted Regents/approved exam results; junior-year class rank or local English/math assessments are allowed alternatives when the specified conditions apply. No universal GPA minimum.
notes: Only eligible New York colleges/universities, not trade schools. Selection methods must be applied consistently; tied nominees are selected by lottery. Attending out-of-state college forfeits the award and later return does not reinstate it. Approved advance one-year delay and limited final-semester/summer payment exceptions apply. Annual renewal requires academic progress.

name: Academic Excellence Scholarship
value: $2,250 per year toward tuition, half state-funded and half institution-matched, for up to eight consecutive semesters or completion of the bachelor’s degree, whichever comes first. No summer payments. Renewal requires 3.0 college GPA and 24/48/72 credits for the second/third/fourth year; specified regain and exception rules apply.
deadline: School nomination is required. Published 2026 nomination window was February 18 to March 13, 2026; 2027 nomination dates have not been published. Enroll full time by September 30 of the academic year after designation; confirm earlier school deadlines.
apply: Public/private high schools designate their highest-GPA eligible seniors and submit nominations and alternates through authorized HEAB GLASS accounts. Provide requested student contact and college details to the school. Current Act 80 guidance also provides a homeschool qualification route.
eligibility: Wisconsin resident and U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Public/private high-school route selects highest school GPA, with awards based on school enrollment; school’s consistent weighted or unweighted GPA method applies. Current Act 80 guidance allows homeschool students with ACT 33 or SAT 1500. Attend a participating Wisconsin UW, technical, independent or tribal institution full time.
notes: Only participating Wisconsin institutions. Current Act 80 rules replace older small-school allocation restrictions; consult HEAB for homeschool processing. Renewal and credit requirements apply; campus-certified exceptions and regain rules are specified in HEA 9.

provider: New Jersey Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA)
name: NJ STARS
value: Published class of 2026 terms: last-dollar tuition for 12-18 degree credits per semester after federal/state grants and scholarships, normally up to five semesters at the home county college. Fees/books excluded. A qualifying 3+1 degree program has a separate first-three-years funding exception; class of 2027 terms are not published.
deadline: Class of 2027 fall 2027 deadlines not published. Historical 2026-27 aid deadlines: renewals April 15, 2026; new fall/spring September 15, 2026; spring-only February 15, 2027. Corresponding NJFAMS task deadlines October 1, 2026 or March 1, 2027. These are not fall 2027 deadlines.
apply: Apply to home county college and file FAFSA or NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application; complete NJFAMS requested tasks and notify the college of NJ STARS eligibility. Use another county college only under the unavailable-program/one-year oversubscription exception.
eligibility: Published class of 2026 terms: New Jersey resident for 12 months before graduation, top 15.0% without rounding at the end of junior or senior year, and qualifying U.S. citizen/noncitizen or NJ Alternative Application eligibility. Full-time 12-18 degree credits at eligible county college; rigorous-course requirement waived for 2026 graduates. Confirm 2027 cohort requirements.
notes: 2026 fact sheet remains the published cohort guidance; 2027 fact sheet not located. Normally start by fifth semester after high-school graduation. Renewal requires continuous full-time enrollment and 3.0 college GPA starting third semester; specified medical/family/military and final-semester exceptions. Summer unfunded; certain sixth-semester engineering/nursing students may retain NJ STARS II eligibility without NJ STARS payment.

name: Opportunity Scholarship
value: Class of 2027 award amount has not been determined; funding depends on appropriations and eligible applicants. The class of 2026 received up to $800 per semester for four semesters ($3,200 total), toward tuition/general fees after other state aid. Confirm the 2027 cohort’s duration and renewal terms when published.
deadline: Class of 2027 applications open January 4, 2027; priority deadline January 29, 2027; final deadline March 18, 2027. Application and student/parent sections of 2027-28 FAFSA must be complete by the applicable deadline. USHE application update email scheduled May 7, 2027. No time zone stated.
apply: Complete USHE online application and 2027-28 FAFSA, including student and required parent sections, by the applicable deadline. Private Utah high-school applicants upload a transcript; qualifying concurrent-enrollment coursework may require an official college transcript. Submit requested verification and follow the eligible college’s enrollment/payment procedures.
eligibility: Class of 2027 graduate of a Utah high school with 3.3 cumulative GPA. Complete three AP/IB/concurrent-enrollment courses in grades 9-12, one each in English, math and science with approved USBE subject codes, before graduation. Complete FAFSA and enroll full time at an eligible Utah institution in fall after graduation unless an approved deferral applies. AP exam scores are not a universal requirement.
notes: Eligible Utah public institutions plus BYU Provo, Ensign, WGU and Westminster. Technical-college attendance can support a deferral rather than immediate scholarship payment. Confirm institution-specific enrollment and payment dates. Current guidance permits specified military, medical, humanitarian, religious-service and technical-study deferrals.

name: Kansas State Scholarship
value: Published 2026-27 funding guidance: up to $1,000 annually ($500 per semester), based on financial need and available funds. Up to four undergraduate years, or five for an approved five-year degree. The 2027-28 funding terms are not confirmed.
deadline: Priority deadline July 1, displayed without a year. School reports scholar designation after seventh-semester grades, generally February-April; ACT by December of senior year. Confirm the 2027 application dates with KBOR.
apply: Complete Kansas Scholars Curriculum and obtain school-certified Kansas State Scholar designation using ACT and seventh-semester GPA index. File FAFSA and State of Kansas Student Aid Application annually, using personal email; upload requested supporting materials. Schools report curriculum completion and academic information; students receive designation notice. Renew through the state aid account.
eligibility: Kansas State Scholar designation and financial need required. Current cohort document names seniors graduating in 2026-27, but is labeled 2026-27 funding guidance; confirm fall 2027 terms. General state rules require Kansas residency for one year before college, eligible Kansas college/program, first undergraduate degree, permanent legal U.S. residence/valid SSN and ability to file FAFSA. No universal high-school GPA minimum.
notes: Renewal guidance requires 3.0 college GPA and at least 12 credits per semester; financial need and outside scholarships affect awards. Document’s aid-year/cohort labels do not establish 2027-28 funding. Designation uses ACT/GPA ranking, not a guaranteed award for every curriculum completer.

name: Roberta B. Willis Need-Merit Scholarship
value: Current overview lists up to $5,250 annually for a four-year program or $4,650 for a two-year program. The detailed FAQ identifies these as AY 2025-26 amounts and states up to six consecutive years; confirm 2027-28 amounts and renewal terms with OHE.
deadline: Counselor-submitted application and FAFSA by February 15th (displayed without a year)
apply: High school counselor submits the application through CT Scholars; student files the FAFSA listing an eligible Connecticut college
eligibility: Connecticut resident with academic merit and allowable annual federal Student Aid Index. High-school seniors may qualify through top 20% of junior class and/or SAT 1200 or ACT 25; undergraduate applicants use eligible high-school senior rank/test routes. Overview specifies eligible four-year Connecticut public/nonprofit institutions; FAQ excludes Yale/Wesleyan while also listing two-year program awards. FAQ’s SAI 10,999 cap is historical, not confirmed for 2027-28.
notes: Need and merit both considered. Current aid overview and historical detailed FAQ were read; confirm 2027-28 SAI cutoff, renewal and eligible-program details. Students cannot submit directly: counselor nomination and FAFSA are required.

name: Boettcher Scholarship
value: $20,000 annually from Boettcher for four consecutive undergraduate years. Public partners supplement up to cost of attendance minus travel/other expenses; private partners supplement up to tuition/fees. Partner support and legal-status eligibility can vary; good standing and continuing lawful presence/status required.
deadline: Explicitly recurring schedule: application opens September 1 and is due November 1 at 5 p.m. during the final high-school year. Closing timezone is not stated. Counselor forms and official transcript due within one week after submission; semifinalists provide two recommendations, finalists interview. Noncitizen approval/affirmation documentation is due August 1 before the award.
apply: Complete online application, essays and activity information. Arrange counselor forms and official transcript within one week after submission; scores optional. Semifinalists provide two recommendation letters; finalists interview. Noncitizens provide status/application evidence at semifinal stage and approved lawful-presence/status documentation and affirmation before award; renew documentation annually.
eligibility: Graduating Colorado high-school student applying in fall of final high-school year, normally Colorado resident for full junior/senior years; federally recognized tribal members with historical Colorado ties have a residency exception. Colorado high-school graduation still required. U.S. citizen, permanent resident or lawfully present, including DACA; applicants in process must document successful status before becoming a Scholar. Relatives of Foundation trustees/officers/employees excluded under published criteria. Merit selection considers academics, leadership, service and character, without financial-need preference.
notes: Only listed four-year nonprofit Colorado partners. Out-of-state binding early decision makes applicant ineligible. Gap-year plans still require applying during final high-school year. Keep Foundation good standing and required annual status affirmation/current lawful-presence documents. Partner matching is not guaranteed for every noncitizen status. Essays should reflect personal experiences and the applicant’s own voice. Sponsor allows AI for brainstorming, outlines and refinement but cautions against heavy reliance and copying an AI-generated essay.

name: Terry Traditional Scholarship
value: Last-dollar support toward university official on-campus cost of attendance after other aid, covering tuition, fees, books and reasonable on-campus living expenses. Up to eight undergraduate semesters, renewed at Foundation discretion subject to requirements; individual stipend varies.
deadline: Affiliated universities set their own admission, scholarship, FAFSA and document deadlines. Texas Tech explicitly publishes October 1, 2026-January 15, 2027 Terry application window, February 1, 2027 FAFSA deadline, February 6 phone screenings and March 29-30 Dallas interviews. Other partners’ full fall-2027 calendars remain unconfirmed. No common statewide date or closing timezone is claimed.
apply: Apply through an affiliated university, not directly to Foundation; complete university admission, scholarship essays, FAFSA and requested documents, then mandatory Foundation interview if nominated. Texas Tech’s current instructions require two essays, recommender email for portal nomination and college transcript for 15 or more completed/planned dual-credit hours. Partner document requirements differ.
eligibility: Graduate of an accredited Texas high school or homeschool; U.S. citizen or permanent resident meeting Texas residency and qualifying for in-state tuition; strong grades and class rank; demonstrated financial need via the FAFSA; leadership record; admitted as a full-time entering freshman; commit to living on campus the first year.
notes: No gap year immediately after high-school graduation; online-only degrees ineligible, at least six semester credits must be attended physically on affiliated campus. First year at nominating university before scholarship can transfer among affiliates. Renewal requires 12 credits each consecutive nonsummer semester, cumulative GPA 2.5 and semester GPA 2.0, annual FAFSA/verification/outside-aid review, required Foundation events, code/handbook compliance and annual self-evaluation by June 1. First-year designated on-campus residence required; campus-specific exceptions apply. Texas Tech’s application calendar is explicitly dated for 2027, but its eligibility section retains a conflicting 2026-27 admission-year label; verify that campus-year detail. Its first-year Terry housing is Murray Hall.

provider: Deseret News and KSL Broadcast Group
name: Sterling Scholar Awards
value: 2026-27 Wasatch Front handbook: regional category winner $2,500; each of two runners-up $1,000; additional General Sterling Scholar $2,500, Gail Miller Service $2,000 or Farnsworth $1,000. Other regions and college awards vary. College benefits table is labeled 2026-27, so 2027-28 college amounts/renewal terms remain unconfirmed.
deadline: Wasatch Front: release forms/photos/captions due December 18, 2026; portfolios close January 11, 2027 at midnight, with no time zone stated. Semifinal notification February 2, 2027; interview/final dates remain TBD. Earlier school nomination deadlines and other regions’ 2027 schedules vary and need confirmation.
apply: School principal nominates one student per category, with only one category per student. Coordinator creates online profile and enters transcript/scores; student uploads signed parent/student release, photo, teacher recommendation, activity lists, category/leadership/service/unique-qualities/life-enrichment essays and category work. Wasatch Front handbook says all uploaded portfolios proceed at cutoff; use coordinator review before closing. Required in-person interviews follow.
eligibility: Utah public high-school students graduating in 2027 and nominated by the school, including eligible concurrent-college and foreign-exchange students. Fourteen categories evaluate academics, category expertise, leadership, service/citizenship and interview; no universal GPA cutoff. Category-specific work and performance requirements apply.
notes: Five independent regional competitions with no statewide round. Current Wasatch Front handbook confirms 2027 activity but some copied payment/college-table sections still label 2026-27. Claim Wasatch cash award by sending college acceptance, student ID and school contact details; funds may be held up to three years for approved delays. College awards require separate campus admission/proof and campus renewal rules. Wasatch handbook prohibits AI use in competition and requires in-person interview participation.
